source_text.body:
Run coding agents and experiments overnight while asleep
OpenClaw drove coding agents from 12:30AM to 7AM, and another user's overnight cron spawns experiment subagents whose results he reviews each morning as decision records.
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
Nathan Clark let OpenClaw manage coding agents from 12:30AM to 7AM. The agent had watched him code all day, so it knew the project's headaches, decisions and history. A separate entry describes Aman Singh's version: he records ideas during the day, and an overnight cron spawns scientist subagents to run experiments. He reviews them each morning and captures decisions as ADR-style records.
How it went
Clark got over 6 hours of autonomous, project-aware coding. He says it drives better than Ralph because it has watched him all day. The source gives no output numbers for Singh's pipeline.
Worth knowing
The advantage depends on the agent observing your work all day, so it needs persistent daytime context. A cold-start overnight loop won't have that.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Set up a nightly job at [time, e.g. 12:30 AM] that works on [project or repo] while I sleep. It should start coding agents on the top items from [my task list or backlog], and for any open question it should run a small experiment and write a short decision record covering what was tried, the result, and a recommendation. Have it all ready as a morning summary by [7 AM], and do not merge, deploy, or delete anything without my approval.
Original source: https://openclawlab.xyz/use-cases/uc-099/
